exposure: Previous exposure to anesthesia (in uterus, first years of life, or later)
Method of childbirth (vaginal delivery vs. cesarean delivery)
Type of anesthesia used during cesarean delivery (general vs. regional)
cohort: The study included 515 children from Puerto Rico, comprising 262 children diagnosed with ASD and 253 non-ASD siblings.
finding: Children exposed to anesthesia, either in uterus, during the first 2 years of life, or later, were not found to be more likely to develop ASD or its severe form.
mod_finding: No statistically significant association was found between the method of childbirth (vaginal vs. cesarean delivery) or the type of anesthesia used during cesarean delivery (general vs. regional) and the development of ASD.
